isolation.code-review-graph: graph database in --data-dir outside the corpus; its registry in an isolated HOME
isolation.codebase-memory: index under an isolated HOME, so the user's own ~/.cache index is untouched
isolation.graft: context directory outside the corpus at /private/tmp/5way/graft-ctx
isolation.graphify: writes graphify-out/ beside the code it reads, so it only ever runs against the private copy at /private/tmp/5way/kena-copy
isolation.kivgraph: isolated HOME at /private/tmp/kivhome-impact; the published generation and the registry live there

code-review-graph.scope: one graph per repository; built the 1 the questions name, not all 37

graft.needs: nothing: the structural tier needs no key and no toolchain

graphify.scope: one graph per repository; built the 1 the questions name, not all 37; run against the private copy, because it writes beside the code it reads
graphify.needs: nothing for the structural pass; a provider key only for the semantic one, which was not measured

kivgraph.scope: the whole corpus, 37 repositories, 126934 symbols published
kivgraph.needs: the Go module cache per indexed module and cargo per Rust workspace; without them a load fails and its symbols are absent

questions.question: Which files hold something that reaches the AutomationScheduledGuildIDs of GuildsHandler within two hops?

code-review-graph.note: impact takes changed files, never a declaration -- `--files internal/application/handlers/guilds_handler.go::GuildsHandler.AutomationScheduledGuildIDs` reports zero changed nodes -- so this is the whole file's reachable set at the selectable --depth 2: 1835 nodes over 69 files; truncated, 1335 nodes omitted

codebase-memory.note: trace_path returned no callers; the answer is the query_graph Cypher fallback over CALLS.

graphify.note: `affected --depth 2` (the flag's own default is 2); graph.json is written `directed: false`, so networkx loads it undirected, affected.py falls back to scanning `graph.edges()` for edges whose stored orientation ends at the seed, and that orientation is node insertion order rather than call direction: the answer is a neighbour set at the given depth, not reverse reachability; `affected "AutomationScheduledGuildIDs"` refused with `No unique node match`, naming none of the 2 nodes whose label contains the name (graphify resolves by label substring, so tests named after the declaration refuse it too); re-asked as the node id `handlers_guilds_handler_automationscheduledguildids`, which is the `{parent_dir}_{stem}_{name}` form the extractor builds and the shipped skill does not document, because graphify has no path-qualified addressing; the node id did not resolve either, so the answer comes from `query`, a depth-2 BFS neighbourhood rather than a reachable set

kivgraph.note: excludes field, variable by default, and says so in the payload

native.note: searched 5330 code files, then read 1 declaring file(s)
